title: 17th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
description: 17th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
summary: The talk argues that Valvoline (VVV) is a compelling investment due to its superior unit economics, disciplined capital allocation, and significant optionality for refranchising and deleveraging. Conversely, the speaker expresses a negative view on AutoZone (AZO), citing share loss in softlines, poor IT systems, and rising leverage. Additionally, the presentation highlights Vail Resorts (VAIL) as an undervalued opportunity with strong pricing power and operating leverage expected to drive earnings reacceleration.
thesis: The talk argues that Valvoline (VVV) is a compelling investment due to its superior unit economics, disciplined capital allocation, and significant optionality for refranchising and deleveraging. Conversely, the speaker expresses a negative view on AutoZone (AZO), citing share loss in softlines, poor IT systems, and rising leverage. Additionally, the presentation highlights Vail Resorts (VAIL) as an undervalued opportunity with strong pricing power and operating leverage expected to drive earnings reacceleration.

claims.claim: Amazon has a strong interest in acquiring UFC media rights as a global popular asset that fits well into their portfolio.
claims.quote: We also spoke with a strategist at Amazon who indicated to us that they have a very strong interest in a global popular asset like the UFC that fits well into their portfolio.
claims.speaker: John

claims.claim: Netflix is a potential buyer of UFC international media rights as part of a bundle deal.
claims.quote: We've seen earlier this year that Netflix acquired WWE's international right as part of the bundle, and they set a precedent that has never happened in industry. From speaking to several experts, Amazon, Eurosport, and ESPN are potential buyers of such a bundle deal.
claims.speaker: Jill

claims.claim: Warner Bros. Discovery is a potential buyer of UFC international media rights as part of a bundle deal.
claims.quote: From speaking to several experts, Amazon, Eurosport, and ESPN are potential buyers of such a bundle deal.
claims.speaker: Jill

claims.claim: Comcast is bidding 2.1 times step up to take Warner Bros.' NBA package from ESPN.
claims.quote: Consensus has the NBA rights going for a two times step up and just this morning, there was a surprise announcement that Comcast was gonna bid a 2.1 times step up and take Warner Bros.' NBA package from that.
claims.speaker: John

claims.claim: Valvoline is positioned to become an industry leader similar to AutoZone and O'Reilly, capable of growing net income while repurchasing shares.
claims.quote: And Valvoline's commitment to returning cash to shareholders, its robust economics, position it to become another industry cannibal like AutoZone and O'Reilly, who've been able to substantially grow net income while strategically repurchasing shares with fuel share price appreciation.

claims.claim: Valvoline's unit economics drive significant cash flow generation, and management is disciplined with capital allocation, planning to buy back approximately 20% of outstanding shares through 2027.
claims.quote: Valvoline's unit economics drive significant cashflow generation, which in the hands of honest management, can create phenomenal returns for investors. This is a management team that has proven that they do not waste cash, and have continued to reiterate their plan of returning capital to shareholders through buybacks. Using both their operational cash flows and its balance sheet, we expect Valvoline to buy back approximately 20% of the outstanding shares through 2027, all while funding their extensive growth plans.

claims.claim: The speaker has a price target of $84 for Valvoline in 2027, based on a base case algorithm of roughly 10% store growth, 8% comp growth, and 25% EPS growth.
claims.quote: Tying all this back into valuation and our $84 price target in 2027, the base case algorithm that gets you there from a 24 to 27 on a CAGR basis is roughly 10% store growth, 8% comp growth, 16% top line growth, around 27% EBITDA margins with high 20s incrementals, so we're not underwriting a lot of margin expansion here, and 25% EPS growth on 70% free cash flow conversion.

claims.claim: Valvoline offers significant optionality for investors, including potential refranchising and deleveraging, which could yield approximately $1.4 billion in incremental value.
claims.quote: And though we didn't consider this in our scenarios, this business offers significant optionality for a proactive investor to take advantage of to increase returns. Not only could Valvoline refranchise its corporate-owned stores, they could also relever. Valvoline's current conservative balance sheet and its history of same-store sales growth and solid free cash flow conversion in the two terms of incremental leverage could potentially yield 1.4 billion in incremental value.

claims.claim: The speaker believes the risk/reward skew for Valvoline is attractively just over three times on base case assumptions, assuming nearly 30% price downside in the variance.
claims.quote: As we mentioned earlier, we do believe that the risk/reward skew attractively here just over three times on our base case assumptions and assuming nearly 30% price downside in our variance.

claims.claim: Valvoline's unit economics are superior to other quick lube peers, and the speaker wrote code to scrape location data to analyze the company's footprint.
claims.quote: And compared to peers, the unit economics are superior to other quick lube peers. - And the franchisees do a combination of own the real estate or lease it. Some of them are like smaller mom and pop investors, like they own five or six and they like having that hard asset, which is the real estate. But when you do a sale leaseback transaction for these, which is a lot of triple nets out there, you just search Valvoline triple net lease, they're all over the place, you really juice the IRR and you can get up to like 40, 45% IRRs, assuming like an exit in five years.

claims.claim: The speaker used their own code in R to scrape location data from Valvoline's website and other major quick lube players to analyze store addresses and map locations.
claims.quote: We wrote our own code in R to essentially scrape location data from Valvoline's website as well as from the other major quick lube players. And when we pulled in that data, we then analyzed essentially the store address. We mapped that using like an API to to Google Maps. We mapped their locations across the U.S. and then we also considered essentially the number of vehicles registered in each state as well as the population density surrounding each Valvoline or Jiffy Lube or Take 5 in a 10-mile radius.

claims.claim: The speaker believes ASO is losing share in softlines vendors like Nike and will face margin compression as its product mix worsens from softlines to hardlines.
claims.quote: So we believe that ASO is losing share in the softlines vendors. So like Nike is obviously one of the largest ones. On the hardlines, so hardlines are like lower margin than softlines, So as you lose share and you sort of like, you know, make your product mix worsen from softlines to hardlines, there'll be a margin compression as well there.
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker holds a negative view on ASO's softline business specifically due to its inability to attract footfall, which will cause weakness in softlines as hardlines are impacted.
claims.quote: To summarize, you know, you're absolutely right, softlines tend to have higher margin and they also have shorter purchase cycles, which is why we see Hibbett and Dick's positioned better. You know, they obviously do softline, but our negative view on softline specifically for ASO comes from the lack of ability to attract footfall, because hardlines will be impacted and therefore, they will have weakness in softlines.
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker thinks ASO has been under-investing in stores, evidenced by poor IT systems that cannot handle pricing common across stores.
claims.quote: Now, the management has been talking about these turnaround initiatives, but we don't think that's enough that can offset these margin pressures. Going ahead, if they reduce their store opening. Now, why we think store opening will happen is that A, that's how the management is incentivized, on absolute sales figures, right? So if your SSSG is is impaired going forward, the only way to offset that is to like keep opening stores, and that's what the management is even guided to.
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker expects ASO's net leverage to rise to 2.5X as EBITDA and FCF decline due to opening new stores in mature markets and impaired cash flow from operations.
claims.quote: So both of these will lead to a much lower FCF, and although the balance sheet is not stressed right now, as our EBITDA declines and as our FCF also declines, we think that going ahead, the net leverage raises to 2.5X. That being said, we don't see the company having to like raise a lot of debt to finance the new store openings because it is making cash right now. So it's not totally impaired and we don't expect it to go to zero, but it will be like significantly stressed going ahead.
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker believes Vail's pricing power and operating leverage will cause earnings growth to reaccelerate, modeling 9% organic free cash flow growth over the next five years.
claims.quote: Our thesis addresses each of these concerns. First, we think that Vail's pricing power, combined with operating leverage, will cause earnings growth to reaccelerate and we model 9% organic free cash flow growth over the next five years. Second, we think that management are wise allocators of capital and while we're excited about potential upside from future acquisitions, we think they'll largely continue returning capital as they already have. And third, we think the weather this season was uniquely bad but also that climate concerns are broadly overblown.
claims.speaker: Joey

claims.claim: The speaker presents a three-year target price of $337 for Vail, which is good for an IRR of 22% including dividends.
claims.quote: Hi. Hi, everyone, I'm Joey. These are my teammates, Erica and Kareem, and today we'll be pitching Vail Resorts as along with a three-year target price of $337, which is good for an IRR of 22% including dividends. Vail owns and operates an irreplaceable network of 41 regional and destination ski resorts, including all four of the most visited destination resorts in North America.
claims.speaker: Joey

claims.claim: The speaker states that Vail's business day run rates are about a 30% EBITDA margin and 65% unlevered free cash flow conversion.
claims.quote: Vail's flagship product, driving a third of revenue, is the Epic Pass. These are only sold at the beginning of each ski season and offer unlimited skiing across all of Vail's resorts. The pre-commitment from Epic Pass customers generates increased visitation, which is important, because ski rental, ski school, dining, and lodging make up 50% of Vail's revenue, and the model overall results in impressive economics. The business day run rates about a 30% EBITDA margin and 65% unlevered free cash flow conversion.
claims.speaker: Joey

claims.claim: The speaker notes that between 2006 and 2018, Vail's stock delivered a 17% IRR and a 6.8X multiple while growing EBITDA at 10% annually and re-rating from 10X to 20X.
claims.quote: Vail has a history of compounding returns for shareholders. Between 2006 and 2018, the stock delivered a 17% IRR and a 6.8X multiple, while growing EBITDA at 10% annually and re-rating from 10X to 20X. Most of this growth came through acquisitions. In 2006 Vail owned just five resorts, and by 2018, they had bought 14 more.
claims.speaker: Joey

claims.claim: The speaker states that since the introduction of the Community Ikon Pass in 2018, the stock has struggled despite Vail growing earnings 44% and expanding its network of resorts to 41.
claims.quote: Since the introduction of the Community Ikon Pass in 2018, the stock has struggled. Despite Vail growing earnings 44% and expanding its network of resorts to 41, the stock is flat because the multiple is Z rated. And today, you can buy Vail for 9.8 times for EBITDA, which is below where it traded for most of the post-GFC period.
claims.speaker: Joey

claims.claim: The speaker believes Vail's stock is undervalued and will re-rate to 11X EBITDA, generating a 22% IRR.
claims.quote: As the market begins to realize this and buy into our first few thesis points, we think the multiple will re-rate to 11X and these three combine to generate our 22% IRR.
claims.speaker: Joey

claims.claim: Vail is expected to compound free cash flow at 9% into 2028 based on 6% revenue CAGR and 4% OpEx CAGR.
claims.quote: We think that Vail can compound free cash flow at 9% into 2028 based on 6% revenue CAGR and 4% OpEx CAGR.
claims.speaker: Kareem

claims.claim: Vail will generate a probability-weighted TSR of 71% or an IRR of 18% by the end of fiscal year 2027.
claims.quote: Our base case assumes an 11X EBITDA multiple, which is about a one turn re-rate from here. and that gets us to a probability-weighted TSR of 71% or an IAR of 18% by the end of fiscal year 2027, which is July, 2027.
claims.speaker: Erica

claims.claim: Vail has the strongest balance sheet compared to competitors like Alterra, Boyne, and Powder, allowing it to outperform in downside scenarios.
claims.quote: Vail has the strongest balance sheet when compared to its other privately owned competitors, such as Alterra, which sells the Ikon pass, Boyne, and Powder.
claims.speaker: Erica

claims.claim: Vail's midwestern and northeastern resorts have nearly 100% of terrain covered by snow-making, enabling quick recovery after negative weather events.
claims.quote: Vail's midwestern and northeastern resort resorts, such as Mount Snow, have nearly 100% of terrain covered by snow-making, which enables them to get back up and running after a negative weather event in under 24 hours.
claims.speaker: Erica

claims.claim: Vail managed to grow EBITDA 8% year-over-year despite unique weather volatility hitting all regions equally hard.
claims.quote: One expert we talked to said that this year was unique and that all of Vail's regions were hit equally hard by weather volatility. We thought this was the most correlated impact likely for Vail given today's climate for the next 10 or 20 years. And despite that, as Kareem mentioned, Vail managed to grow EBITDA 8% year-over-year.
claims.speaker: Erica

claims.claim: Even in draconian climate scenarios, ski seasons are projected to shorten between one and two months, resulting in less than 1% shrinkage per year.
claims.quote: But even in the most draconian scenarios, ski seasons are only projected to shorten between one and two months, which on a five- to six-month total season across 30 plus years, results in less than 1% shrinkage per year.
claims.speaker: Erica

claims.claim: The speaker believes PoolCorp's earnings will miss guidance by 9% due to industry decline, competition, and margin pressure.
claims.quote: Putting all the three factors together, we believe the EPS is going to miss guidance by 9% and the company is going to cut the guidance again during the summer like it did in 2023.

claims.claim: Intensified competition from Heritage and Home Depot will cause a 5% revenue drop and 2% gross margin decline.
claims.quote: This will be translated to 5% drop in revenue and 2% drop in gross margin. PoolCorp used to be a very successful roll-up story, and for the past two decades, they barely had any legitimate competitor.

claims.claim: The speaker believes PoolCorp has limited runway for growth and the roll-up strategy will not work going forward.
claims.quote: But we believe they're a limited runway, because they already capture 40% of the market share and the roll-up strategy will not work going forward.

claims.claim: The speaker assigns a target price of 240 by end of year, implying a 33% downside based on a 18x multiple.
claims.quote: And we assign a target price of 240 by end of this year, which imply a 33% downside and we use 18 times multiple, which is also higher than their pre-COVID 10-year average of 14 times.

claims.claim: Management sold $15 million worth of stock in February, and the speaker believes this represents an asymmetric opportunity to short the stock.
claims.quote: First is management. They just sold $15 million worth of stock, open market, in February this year. And second group, a bunch of short sellers are starting to build up their positions.

claims.claim: The speaker believes PoolCorp has 1 billion debt with debt over EBITDA multiples around 2 and 2.5, maturing in 2026.
claims.quote: So they have currently have 1 billion debt and their debt over EBITDA multiples is around 2 and 2.5, and they just paid their 300 million Q1, and this debt is maturing 2026.

claims.claim: The speaker believes PoolCorp has 17 million of cash and typical OCF of 400 million, generating about 300 million of free cash flow.
claims.quote: So currently their balance sheet has 17 million of cash and their typical OCF is about 400 million, and typically it's 100 million of CapEx. So that would generate about 300 million of free cash flow.

claims.claim: The speaker believes PoolCorp already has 40 sales centers versus Heritage who only have 100, and PoolCorp already got full 40% market share.
claims.quote: So like there's still runway for Heritage, but PoolCorp already got full 40% market share. Where could you go from here? Like they go to 80%?

claims.claim: The speaker believes Heritage was bought as part of SRS, and Heritage was 1/6 of SRS.
claims.quote: It's 1/6. - 1/6. Okay. So maybe not Home Depot's primary bet in acquiring Heritage either, right?
